cards.summary: custom agents (prompt, model, tools, permission) and the default one
cards.text:
An agent is a markdown file: <data dir>/agents/<name>.md or <project>/.mendcode/agents/<name>.md (project agents do nothing until the user trusts the project in /tools; .claude/agents is read too, as data). The body (up to 16,000 characters) is added to the system prompt.
  ---
  name: reviewer            # default: the file name; lowercase letters, digits, _ and -
  description: Reviews a diff without touching it   # required, up to 300 characters
  mode: primary             # primary | subagent | all (default all)
  model: gpt-6-sol          # optional: a catalog model id (see {{program}} models)
  effort: high              # optional: minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh
  tools: [read, grep, glob] # optional allow list; a trailing * matches a prefix (mcp__github__*)
  deny: [shell]             # optional, applied after the allow list
  permission: ask           # optional cap: plan | ask | smart | edits | full
  ---
  You review code. Read what changed, run nothing, edit nothing. Report findings as a list.
Other fields: temperature, top_p, variant, steps (last model call has no tools), hidden (not in the picker), disable, color (hex or a theme role).
Primary agents are what the user switches between (/agent, agent.next in {{program}} docs key-actions); sub-agents are what the task tool starts, or what @name mentions: running, continuing and stopping them is {{program}} docs subagents. build and plan can be overridden by a file of the same name. A new session starts as the default_agent setting (the user's /settings; a project may set its own with defaultAgent), build when unset or unknown. Agent files apply to the native engine only: sessions on Claude Code or Codex models ignore them.
Without a file, the daemon setting agent (a map by agent name) overrides fields of an agent. Manage from the CLI: {{program}} agent list | create | debug. The user sees all agents and problems in /agents and /doctor.

cards.summary: images, PDFs and files in a message; read images; generate images; voice
cards.text:
For: "attach this image / PDF / folder", "look at this screenshot", "what is in this picture", "make an image", "dictate instead of typing".

The user's way: /attach <path> (project files insert @path; an external text file is inlined up to 200 KiB; an external folder becomes a sorted listing), drop or paste a path, or the clipboard key for an image. It enters the prompt as a token at the cursor ([Image #1], [PDF name.pdf]); pasted images may be up to 20 MiB, PDFs 5 MiB. Profile key attachmentChips inline|above|both; images auto|kitty|iterm2|sixel|off chooses how the terminal draws images.

Model tools:
  read {path}: text, folders, PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP and PDFs (inline images and PDFs up to 5 MiB; 2,000 lines by default, long lines cut at 2,000 characters).  screenshot (macOS only): the screen, front window or a region as an image, at most 1600 px; asks for approval.
  image_gen {prompt, size?, n?, path?, referenced_image_paths?}: only for an explicit image request; uses the separate image provider and model (daemon setting image_generation, also needed by the pet generator); it writes managed artifacts or a path inside the project and never overwrites; approval applies. In a Claude Code session it is mcp__mendcode__image_gen (feature harness_tools) and works unconfigured with the ChatGPT login or a saved OpenAI key; never send the user to another engine for an image.
  While an image is generated its card is an animated ASCII canvas with the model and size (/customize, section Image generation: imageWait animated|static, imageWaitPreset drops|cycle|constellation|orbit|pulse|scanner or a name from imageWaitArt, imageWaitSpeed ms per frame, imageWaitColor, imageWaitMeta; imageWaitArt and imageWaitCanvas in tui/profile.json). Reduced motion holds its first frame.

Voice: /voice or ctrl+x v starts recording, again stops and puts the transcript in the prompt to review (esc drops the clip). Full tier; the user turns it on with /voice on (voice.enabled). The clip is uploaded to an OpenAI-compatible transcription endpoint, so it is opt-in; a ChatGPT login is not an API key and does not work. It needs an installed recorder (rec/sox, arecord, ffmpeg); /voice status says what is missing. Setting voice: provider, model, base_url, language (es), max_seconds 5 to 300.

Data honesty: an attachment is read by the model only when it is sent; a path outside the project is read only if the user attached it. If the image or PDF did not load, say so; do not describe what you did not see.

Not possible: sending a file to another program or user from here (use the shell under approvals); listening to the microphone without /voice on.

Check: the token or chip appears in the prompt; read of an image returns an image, not text.

cards.summary: run MendCode headless: scripts, CI, JSON output, GitHub, editors, HTTP
cards.text:
For: "run it from a script / cron / CI", "get the answer as JSON", "limit what it can do in a job", "use it from GitHub", "build my own client".

Shortest path: {{program}} run "message" (piped stdin is appended; a stdin silent for 1 s is skipped unless - is given; run - uses stdin only). It starts the daemon if needed, runs one turn and exits.
  Choose: --model provider/model, --agent NAME, --variant NAME, --effort minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh, --permission ask|edits|plan|smart (never full), --cwd PROJECT, --dir DATA, -f FILE… (files, images, a directory listing; the message may follow), --command NAME.
  Narrow it for a job: --tools a,b (allow-list; never grants more than the rules allow; sub-agents off), --exclude-tools, --offline (no webfetch, websearch, image_gen), --max-turns N, --add-dir PATH, --system-prompt TEXT, -c KEY=VALUE.
  Output: --format json streams raw events; --output-schema FILE makes stdout one validated JSON document; -o FILE writes the final message; --ephemeral deletes the session after.
  Exit codes of run: 0 done, 1 failed, 2 stopped, 3 answer rejected by the schema, 4 --max-turns reached, 5 an approval was denied for lack of --approve and nothing ran after it, 64 usage error.
  Nobody answers approvals in a script: --approve approves once, --dangerously-skip-permissions approves everything (also what Claude Code flags): only with the user's say-so, in a sandbox they chose. Both are the user's: from your own shell they are refused, and a session you start there gets at most your session's permission mode.
Background: run --bg returns the session id at once; ps lists, logs ID [-f] follows, kill ID cancels, attach ID opens the TUI on it. {{program}} session ... and {{program}} apply [SESSION] --to DIR (all-or-nothing copy of a session's file changes) exist too.
GitHub: {{program}} github install writes the workflow that answers comments mentioning its trigger words, github run executes one event; publishing and approvals are opt-in ({{program}} docs git).
Editors and other UIs: {{program}} acp is a stdio agent for Zed or JetBrains; {{program}} app-server is a JSON-RPC server (threads, turns, approvals) for third-party UIs, local-only; {{program}} generate prints the socket schema, generate --httpapi the OpenAPI contract of the opt-in HTTP adapter (daemon --http-listen 127.0.0.1:9877, loopback, bearer token). Remote use: {{program}} docs remote.

Commands take --json and --dir DATA; {{program}} help lists them. A bad flag is a usage error (exit 64) before any session exists; a daemon too old for --tools fails the run instead of running unrestricted.

Not possible: an unattended job that is asked for approval and waits (it needs --approve or a --permission mode that fits); full access from --permission; a script that changes the user's trust or credentials.

Check: the exit code and, with --json, the final event; say which you read.

cards.summary: long commands, servers, watchers and interactive programs in the background
cards.text:
For: "start the dev server and tell me when it is ready", "run the build while you keep going", "watch this log", "run a REPL / installer that asks questions", "what is still running".

Background shell commands:
  shell {command, background: true}: returns a task id at once and keeps running. Approvals as for a foreground command; its timeout (120 s, at most 600 s) does not apply.
  shell_output {id, waitMs?, until?}: new output since the last read, status and exit code; waitMs (at most 30000) waits for output or exit; until: "exit" waits for the end only (120 s, at most 600 s); no id lists this session's tasks. task_status {id} peeks at the end without moving the read position. Binary output is one line with its size.
  shell_monitor {id, match?, stop?}: pushes output lines that contain any of up to 8 texts (case-insensitive substrings, no regex; every line when none) as messages in 2 s batches of at most 20 lines. For "ready or errors": match ["ready","error"]; it ends when the task exits, on stop, or after 30 messages.
  shell_kill {id}: SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 2 s; no exit message follows.
  When a task ends on its own you get one message with the end of its output (not if shell_output already showed its exit): after your next tool result in the running turn, or in a new turn if your answer ended first (always with a non-native engine). Keep working; use until: "exit" only when nothing else can be done first. Do not poll or sleep.
Limits: 8 running tasks across all sessions; 256,000 characters kept per task (older output scrolls out; the next read says how much); a task running after 6 hours is stopped; 32 finished tasks stay readable. A session only sees and stops its own tasks.

Programs that ask questions or need a terminal (installers, REPLs, debuggers, ssh): shell_session {action: start|write|read|resize|signal|kill|list}. macOS and Linux only; at most 4 per chat and 8 in all; idle 15 minutes stops it, 2 hours at most; a bare shell (bash, zsh with no script) is refused: use shell per command.

Read-only jobs: with the user's experimental.async_tools on, tool_start {tool: read|grep|glob|webfetch}, tool_status, tool_wait, tool_cancel run them while you continue (4 active, 8 queued per session); question_start/question_status do the same for questions (experimental.async_questions). Shell and writes cannot.

After the user cancels a turn, notices of tasks that end arrive with the user's next message; the chat shows them as one line, ctrl+s sends them now.

User: Jobs dock (ctrl+t); /ps stops tasks (read: killed (user)); /bg detaches the session ({{program}} docs subagents).

Not available: a task that outlives the daemon (a stop or restart ends it); auto-restart of a task; input to a plain background task (use shell_session); live output on the user's screen other than the dock and the transcript card.

Check: shell_output shows running or the exit code. A server that should listen: confirm with a request or its log, not the task id.

cards.summary: project backlog: the user's own pending items, kept across sessions
cards.text:
For: "what is pending in this project", "put that on my list", "what did we leave undone", "add it to the backlog".

What it is: the user's own list of pending things for a project (full tier; /tier backlog on|off). It survives sessions and daemon restarts. It is not your todo tool (your working checklist for this session), not /scratch (a private note) and not memory.

Read it, when the user asks about pending work or before proposing what to do next:
  {{program}} backlog list --json
prints { directory, items: [{ id, text, done, createdAt, doneAt?, origin?: { sessionId?, path?, commit? } }] } for the directory the command runs in, open items first. Without --json: one line per item, "#3 [ ] text  (file · commit · session id)". "the project backlog is off" means the feature is off: say so, the user turns it on.

You never write it. add, done, reopen, remove and clear are refused from a session's own shell, by the command and by the daemon. Do not look for another way (the file under the data directory is the user's).

Proposing an item: when a turn ends with something left undone, or you notice work outside the request, say it in plain text, one line each:
  Left undone: <one line the user can paste, 300 characters at most>
and tell the user the command: /backlog add <text> (they may add --file PATH and --commit SHA so it opens from where it was born). The item exists only once they add it. Never say it was added.

When the user finishes something that is on the list, name the item and its number so they can type /backlog done <id>.

The user types: /backlog (the list) · /backlog add [--file PATH] [--commit SHA] <text> · /backlog done|reopen|remove <id> · /backlog open <id> (switches to the session it was added in and opens its file) · /backlog clear (removes the finished ones). Card in the right panel: /panel widget backlog. Headless: {{program}} backlog list|add|done|reopen|remove|clear [--json].

Limits: 200 items per project, one line of 300 characters each; numbers are never reused.

Not possible: a model tool for the list; items per session; due dates, priorities or assignees; sharing a list between projects.

cards.summary: spend limits, token prices and usage figures
cards.text:
The daemon setting budgets: { "mode": "subscription" | "api-usage", "warnUsd", "stopUsd", "expensiveModelRequiresConfirm", "prices", "suppliedUsd" }. Default is subscription with no thresholds. Empty thresholds disable that threshold; amounts are finite and non-negative; stopUsd is at least warnUsd.
  { "mode": "api-usage", "warnUsd": 1, "stopUsd": 3, "expensiveModelRequiresConfirm": true,
    "prices": { "provider:model": { "input": 1, "output": 2, "cacheRead": 0.1, "cacheWrite": 1.5, "expensive": true } } }
Prices are explicit local USD per million tokens, keyed by the exact catalog model id; nothing is guessed, and a call without a known price is counted as unknown, never free. Known spend is the lifetime cost for the data dir (<data dir>/budget/spend.json) plus any suppliedUsd.
Read: {{program}} control-plane budget status | doctor; usage over time: {{program}} usage [--days N] [--models] [--tools N]; the user has /usage and /status. Change: the user's /setup (mode, thresholds, confirmation) or /settings, or mendcode_settings propose {"budgets":{...}} (the whole object), saved only on the user's Apply. A limit is the user's decision: never raise or remove one unless the user asked for that exact change.
The prompt's own cost per call: {{program}} docs prompt-modes. Provider quota windows (5h, weekly) and context: {{program}} docs usage. /stats-project inspects this project's usage.
When a provider limit stops a turn (feature usage_resume, on in every tier) the turn is paused, not lost: the transcript says when the window resets and the daemon resumes the same conversation then, even after a restart. The user's /limit shows, snoozes, resumes or cancels it; esc cancels when idle. Peers cannot schedule or resume it. Turning it off affects new pauses only.

cards.summary: how long Anthropic keeps the prompt cache: 5m or 1h, and Claude Code's
cards.text:
For: "keep the Anthropic cache longer", "my cache expires while the tests run", "1h cache", "does Claude Code get the 1h cache".

Anthropic keeps a cached prompt prefix 5 minutes after the last call that read or wrote it, or 1 hour when the request asks for it. A 1h write costs 2x the input price, a 5m write 1.25x; a read costs a tenth of the input price or less either way. Native engine only, on the Anthropic API and Claude on Vertex; every other provider is left as it is.

The user sets it in /settings, Behavior, row "cache ttl" (or you propose it with mendcode_settings; it saves on the user's Apply): promptCacheTtl 5m (default, every tier) | 1h. It is read at each call. A host that refuses the field gets the same call again without it, once, and that session stays at 5 minutes.

Full tier, while the row says 5m (the user's /tier wait_cache on|off): a session whose calls were twice more than 5 and at most 60 minutes apart (a long test run, a slow answer from the user) writes at 1h from the second such call on. A wait past an hour puts it back at 5m. It learns from waits already seen; nothing can know that the next reply will start a long command. Sub-agent calls inside a session learn on their own. A daemon restart forgets it.

Worth it when waits of 5 to 60 minutes repeat: each one then reads the prefix instead of rewriting it at 1.25x. One such wait after the switch repays the higher write price. Steady work that never pauses 5 minutes gains nothing from 1h and only pays more per write.

Compaction while idle follows the call: after one written at 1h it starts 59 minutes later instead of 4. {{program}} context "$MENDCODE_SESSION_ID" says when ({{program}} docs compaction).

Claude Code as the engine manages its own cache. /settings row "claude ttl" (claudeCacheTtl, off in every tier): with cache ttl at 1h, each new Claude Code process is started with CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h (Claude Code 2.1.242 or later). At 5m nothing is passed and Claude Code keeps its defaults: on a subscription the main conversation already gets an hour, its sub-agents 5 minutes.

How long it has left, full tier, off until placed ([[feature:cache_countdown]]; the user runs /footer +warm, or /tier cache_countdown on outside full): "cache 12m", "cache cold · next sends 161K" after; "~" when the lifetime is assumed (ChatGPT). Where expiries cost: /usage tab Waste, {{program}} stats --waste.

Not possible: a lifetime other than 5m or 1h; a longer lifetime on OpenAI, ChatGPT, Bedrock or any other provider; pings that keep a cache warm.

cards.summary: find symbols and callers by graph, language servers, and the code map card
cards.text:
For: "who calls this function", "where is X defined", "what breaks if I change this file", "give me the structure of the project", "type errors".

Model tools (TS/JS/Py/Go/Rust/Swift; read-only, no approval; feature codegraph, tier balanced; MENDCODE_CODEGRAPH=0 turns it off; the live line says if on):
  graph_find {query, kind?, path?, limit?, source?}: ranked symbols with file:line; Class.method works; source: true adds up to 8 numbered lines per match.
  graph_callers {symbol, direction: in|out, depth: 1-20|"all", path?}: call chains. graph_file_api {path}: one file's symbols with line spans, exports and imports.
  graph_map {path?, depth?}: directories with file counts per language and the 20 hub symbols. graph_impact {path, depth?}: cached transitive callers and import dependents; never rebuilds the index.
  code_search {query, path?}: text hits with file:line from jg when installed, else the graph fallback (its reason is in the result).
  lsp {operation, filePath, line, character, query?}: semantic goToDefinition, findReferences, hover, documentSymbol, workspaceSymbol, goToImplementation and call hierarchy from the project's language servers; diagnostics lists their errors. Servers start from .mendcode/lsp.json (false disables); a request times out after 4 s.
All results are bounded (50 rows).

When: ask the graph before reading many files, and the language server when correctness matters. A caller list is a map, never proof that nothing else calls it: dynamic dispatch, callbacks, tsconfig paths, object-literal methods and a second declaration on one line are not resolved. Say that limit when the answer depends on it, and confirm with lsp, a grep or the tests.

Indexed on a graph call or m in /panel galaxy, never home or up. auto: git repo folders under 10,000 files; elsewhere graph tools are unlisted (footer: graph off · reason). /graph on|off|auto: this project; /graph default: all (codegraph_index). Orientation is off by default: /tier graph_context on (balanced, full) adds a code map of the project (directories, files, hubs) once per session, drawn as a card or one row; the profile key codeMapCard auto|open|folded sets the card (ctrl+o or a click opens one).

Data honesty: the index is a cache per project built from files on disk; a symbol added a moment ago may be missing until the next scan, and a file changed after indexing returns no source excerpt. The cap is 20,000 indexed files. If a tool says it is unavailable, use grep and read, and say you did.

Formatting: successful write, edit and apply_patch calls format the written file when .mendcode/formatter.json enables it (true for the builtins, or custom argv commands with $FILE; off when absent), then report errors of running language servers; an installed one starts in the background after a write (MENDCODE_LSP_WARMUP=0: off). A failure appends a Formatting: section to the tool result; the edit still succeeded.

Check: every hit has file:line; read the line before relying on it.

cards.summary: the built-in slash commands, hide/pin/alias them; add a custom command
cards.text:
Built-in slash commands are typed by the user (Tab completes, Enter runs); the model cannot type them. The list below is this install's: its tier, the commands it offers by menu group (name=alias), what the profile hides, pins or moves, the user's own commands and aliases, and what the next tier adds. {{program}} docs commands <name> prints one command.
Set up the menu: <data dir>/tui/profile.json, key slashCommands, a list with one entry per command (only name is required):
  { "name": "changes", "aliases": ["d"], "pinned": true, "hidden": false, "group": "code", "order": 2 }
aliases: up to 8 lowercase words (letters, digits, - _) that run the command with its arguments (alias d on changes: the user types the alias, then arguments, and /changes runs with them); never a built-in's name or alias, never used twice. hidden: true takes it out of the menu's browsing (typing still finds it and it runs); hidden: false lists one the tier leaves out. pinned: first in its group and in recent. group: session|context|code|agents|setup|look|more. order: 0..10000 within the group. A word that was a built-in alias once is no command: it answers "/<word> is now /<command>".
Apply: customize_ui {"action":"settings","values":{"slashCommands":[{ "name": "changes", "aliases": ["d"] }]}} (in minimalist find the tool with tool_search). The value REPLACES the whole list: send every entry to keep, from "slashCommands now" below. It is validated (an error changes nothing), saved and applied live to every open terminal. Undo: send the old list, or {{program}} control-plane tui rollback. Editing the file by hand also works and applies on the next start. The user's way: /customize > Slash menu > Edit commands (h hides, p pins, arrows regroup).
A command that computes something (a UUID, the branch) with no model turn: {{program}} docs extend. A prompt command is a markdown file: <data dir>/commands/<name>.md (or <project>/.mendcode/commands/<name>.md, which wins). Typed as /<name>; a subfolder becomes folder:name. The body is the prompt template.
  ---
  description: Review the diff of a branch
  argument-hint: <branch>
  ---
  Review the changes of $1 against main. Point out bugs first.
Frontmatter: description, argument-hint, agent, model, subtask (true runs it as a sub-agent). $ARGUMENTS is everything after the name, $1..$9 the quoted words; with no placeholder the arguments are appended. @path inlines a file; !`cmd` embeds a command's output (through normal permissions; project ones need /tools trust). Templates are capped at 32,000 characters.
Without a file: a "command" map in mendcode.json (data dir or project root): { "command": { "audit": { "description": "...", "template": "Review $ARGUMENTS", "agent": "explore", "subtask": true } } }. An enabled skill also runs as /<skill-name>. A command never replaces a built-in. /doctor lists commands that fail or are shadowed.
Everything the program offers outside a session is a CLI command: {{program}} help.

For: "I want to comment on one paragraph", "answer option 2 and 3 differently", "give feedback on part of your answer".

The user's flow (no model tool starts it): select a passage with the mouse (copy-on-select) and press ctrl+g (works in every terminal; alt+q and ctrl+x w do the same) or click the pill on the prompt's top rule; Enter stores the comment as a chip above the prompt and a mark in the margin; up to nine; Enter on the prompt sends the chips and the typed text as one message, and with an empty prompt only the comments. alt+l lists them (e edits, d deletes). cards.summary: context getting full: compaction, snip, context window, prompt cache
cards.text:
For: "the context is filling up", "why did it forget", "when does it compact".

Read numbers, never guess: {{program}} context "$MENDCODE_SESSION_ID" (--json: limits) prints the model, window and its source, where it compacts and why, tokens in context. {{program}} models [provider] --verbose: contextWindow, maxContextWindow, compactAtTokens.

Window: the session's /context-window 200k|1m|128000|reset (1,000 to 10,000,000), else the model's modelContext, else the model list. For every session on the model: /context-window 500k --always (reset --always), never above its known maximum ({{program}} docs models).
Compaction point, the first set, never above the window: compaction.token_limit of the model's or provider's providers.json entry; MENDCODE_COMPACT_AT_TOKENS of the daemon; compactAt of modelContext; compactAtTokens (8,000 to 2,000,000); token_limit of compaction. None set: threshold percent of the window (default 95). No window stated: 160,000.
Claude Code (claude_compact, balanced): compacts at that point, else 200k; /compact runs its own.
For every session: /settings, Behavior, row "compact at" (450k; "default" clears), or propose {"compactAtTokens":450000} with mendcode_settings. compaction { auto (false: only /compact), threshold, token_limit, tail_turns, prune, strategy, ... } has no row.
While idle (full tier; /tier idle_compact on|off): a native session of idleCompactAtTokens tokens or more (default 100000; /settings row "idle compact") compacts once just before the provider's prompt cache expires; the context command says when or why not. Other providers: cacheLifetimeMinutes {id: minutes}.
Notice (/tier compact_notice off): at compactNoticePercent percent of the point (80; "off"; /settings row "compact notice") the transcript says once the tokens and turns left.

The user types: /compact queues a compaction behind running work. /compaction reopens the latest: progress, written memory, a note run once after. /context shows what fills the window; /files lists the files in context. Near a usage limit a checkpoint is saved (/tier limit_checkpoint off); /limit resumes ({{program}} docs usage).

What survives: a checkpoint summary (goal, request, decisions, files, commands, todos) plus the last turns; the transcript stays in /timeline and /export. What it dropped: re-read the file or ask, never guess; with /experimental auto_recall on, matching earlier turns return verbatim after each request. handoffTokenCap: earlier conversation another engine gets after a switch (16000; 0 off).

Model tool: snip (/experimental snip on): alone it lists the largest tool outputs; with ids it replaces them by a note; the cache restarts from the first.

Prompt cache: promptCache legacy (default) | off | smart (a key per compaction lineage); cache and cacheProjects narrow it by project, session, provider. A compaction changes the prefix: the next call is a cache miss.

Not possible: compacting from a tool; undoing it; per-message "forget" except snip.

cards.summary: control the screen and apps (macOS), or drive a headless browser
cards.text:
For: "open the Notes app and type something", "click that button", "test my site in a browser", "take a screenshot of the window". Two different things; pick by target.

A real macOS app: the computer tools (feature computer, macOS only). They are off until the user runs /tier computer on (no restart; no tier turns them on); if they are missing, say so and name that switch instead of falling back to screenshot. Disabled means no helper, no compile, no capture, no OS prompt. First use compiles a small Swift helper with Apple's Command Line Tools (xcode-select --install) and needs two macOS permissions for the terminal or daemon: Accessibility, and Screen Recording for captures. MendCode never grants them itself, and approval inside MendCode is separate from the OS permission.
  computer_session {action: apps|start|stop, ...}: lists GUI apps (no activation) and opens a session on one. computer_observe {computerSessionID, screenshot?}: a revisioned accessibility tree of the app. computer_code {computerSessionID, code}: a short confined program of operations (click, type, keys) that keeps one input lease. computer_capture {region?, windowID?} and computer_key {captureID, key} for screenshots and navigation keys. Binding an app asks once in the modes that ask; full access binds and acts without a card. A restart or cancel never replays an action. In a browser a plain click on a link, tab or label presses it.
  screenshot (plain macOS tool): the screen, the front window or a region as an image, at most 1600 px.

A web page or your dev server: the browser tool (feature browser, tier full, the user's MENDCODE_BROWSER=1; tools: { browser: false } turns it off per project). It launches the Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave already installed (MENDCODE_BROWSER_PATH picks one), headless, with a throwaway profile; it is not the user's own browser and has none of their logins.
  browser {action: navigate|snapshot|click|type|press|scroll|back|wait|screenshot|console|close, plus tabs, open_tab, select_tab, close_tab}: snapshot gives page text and numbered elements ([3] button "Save"); click and type take that ref and go stale after navigation, so snapshot again. Passwords and one-time-code fields are never shown. Downloads are denied; dialogs are dismissed. Limits: 8 tabs per chat, 4 chats with a browser, idle 10 minutes closes it.

Before promising either: read "On this machine now". If it says off, say what is off and the switch (/tier computer on; MENDCODE_BROWSER=1 when the daemon starts, full tier, for the browser); do not substitute osascript or a shell script for a click without telling the user.

Not possible: Windows or Linux desktop control; reading the user's browser tabs or logins; typing into password fields of the page.

Approvals for each action: {{program}} docs permissions.

Check: observe or snapshot after each action and compare with what was meant; if a permission is missing the tool says which.

The look of the terminal is a profile (<data dir>/tui/profile.json): theme, density, view, prompt box and border, logo, tagline, home layout, footer, sidebar, markdown style, pet, slash menu, and about 190 more keys.

Which key changes a part: customize_ui {"action":"keys","query":"top bar"} returns the matching keys, what each does, its values and the value now; every part of the screen and its key: {{program}} docs screen-parts.
Not in your tool list (minimalist): tool_search finds customize_ui. The result lists errors; a bad key or value changes nothing and names the nearest keys.
All keys, types, defaults and allowed values at once: {{program}} control-plane tui schema

Presets (the user's terminal; from your shell use customize_ui, the CLI only reads): {{program}} control-plane tui apply-preset compact|comfortable|spacious|toggle-worktree. The user's way: /customize (a page with every control and a live preview), /theme, /view.

cards.summary: run a session on Claude Code, pi or an ACP agent; the thread bridge
cards.text:
For: "use my Claude Code / pi / Gemini CLI as the model", "add an ACP agent", "let Claude Code call a MendCode sub-agent". An engine is who runs the turn; tier, prompt mode and permission mode are separate.

Pick the model in /model and that session's turns go to the engine behind it; native MendCode tools, memory and prompts are then NOT in play, the engine's own are. What stays MendCode's: the transcript, approvals (its permission modes map onto the engine's), esc to stop, the sessions list.

Claude Code: the models claude-fable, claude-opus, claude-sonnet, claude-haiku show in /model only when `claude --version` answers on the daemon's PATH (MENDCODE_CLAUDE_BIN names the binary, MENDCODE_CLAUDE=0 hides them). Those are aliases for the newest of each family; a full id of a family (claude-haiku-5-5, claude-opus-5-5, a dated id) pins the session to that model, anything else is an unknown model. It uses its own login (claude auth login) and its own CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks and MCP servers; MendCode never reads its credentials. One claude process per session (stops after 10 idle minutes). "Always" approvals last this session. The 5h and 7d windows show in /usage; no cost is shown (subscription).

pi (feature pi, tier full, permit: off until opted in): create <data dir>/pi.json ({} is enough) or the user's /tier pi on. Models come from pi; the sign-in is inside pi, with pi's own login command. --safe-mode turns it off. Nothing starts until a turn is sent on a pi model.

ACP agents (Gemini CLI, Zed's adapters, codex-acp and others): the user's /acp page (a adds, e edits, d removes, r refreshes), the setting acpAgents or <data dir>/acp-agents.json { "name": { "command", "args", "env" } }; the model is acp:<name>, plus acp:<name>/<model> per model the agent offered on its first turn (kept in <data dir>/acp-models.json). OpenCode's free models: /connect → OpenCode (free) adds `opencode acp`. Full tier: /tier acp_registry on adds an offline catalog (c on /acp; never installs or probes). Remote clients cannot edit agents or run their turns.

Thread bridge (feature thread_mcp, tier full): lets Claude Code, Codex or an ACP agent call MendCode sub-agents. Off by default, one opt-in each: the user runs /tier thread_mcp on claude|codex|acp:<name> (threadMcp); new turns get delegate_task, whose task_id + model moves a child to another model with its history.

On this machine: read "On this machine now". An engine model missing from /model is almost always the binary not on the daemon's PATH, not logged in, or the feature off; `{{program}} models` shows the catalog.

Not possible: mixing an engine's tools into a native turn, using Codex or Claude credentials from MendCode, an engine that was withdrawn (OpenCode, Cursor SDK: removed, not coming back without an official protocol). Docs do not describe a Codex engine setup; say so rather than guess.

cards.text:
For: "add a hola slash command", "a tool that counts lines", "block rm -rf", "never read private/", "play a sound when a turn ends", "log every tool call", "always answer in Spanish", "today's date in the context", "add provider X". Do it now, live, in one TypeScript file; never answer with a promise to behave.
Tool: mendcode_extend (find it with tool_search). {"action":"write","file":"hola.ts","content":"<module>"} writes <data dir>/extensions/hola.ts, loads it, returns what it registered or its errors (fix: {"action":"edit","file","old","new"}). {"action":"command","text":"/<name> args"} runs a command. A guard's write takes "checks":[{"tool":"shell","args":{"command":"cat private/a"},"expect":"block"},{"tool":"read","args":{"path":"a.md"},"expect":"allow"}], tried at once.
  export default { name: "hola", daemon(api) {
    api.registerCommand({ name: "hola", description: "git branch", run: async (args, { cwd }) => ({ notice: (await api.exec("git", ["branch", "--show-current"], { cwd })).stdout.trim() }) })
  } }
run returns { notice } (shown, no turn) or { prompt } (sent to the model).
Model tool: api.registerTool({ name: "count_lines", description, permission: "read", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { path: { type: "string" } }, required: ["path"] }, execute: async (args, { cwd }) => ({ output: "7" }) }); resolve paths against cwd.
Guard: api.on("tool.before", (e) => /\brm\s+-\w*(rf|fr)/.test(String(e.args.command ?? "")) ? { block: "rm -rf is blocked" } : undefined). e.tool: shell, read, write, edit, apply_patch, grep, glob, ls; e.args.command, e.args.path, e.cwd. A path rule tests JSON.stringify(e.args); shell and grep calls are also asked as a read of each path. { args } rewrites a call; tool.after (e.output) rewrites a result.
Input: api.on("input", (e) => e.text.trim() === "lgtm" ? { text: "Looks good. Commit." } : undefined).
Prompt: fixed text for every session: <data dir>/APPEND_SYSTEM.md, no code. Changing text: api.on("prompt.system", (e) => e.system + "\nToday is " + new Date().toDateString()).
Events: api.on("turn.end" | "turn.start" | "session.start", (e) => ...) with e.sessionId, e.cwd, e.outcome. Sound: spawn("afplay", ["/System/Library/Sounds/Glass.aiff"]) from node:child_process.

cards.summary: TypeScript extensions: slots, keys, pages, views, daemon hooks
cards.text:
An extension is one .ts or .js file in <data dir>/extensions/ (also extensions/<name>/index.ts). Adding a file adds the feature; deleting it removes it. Layers: user packages, user folder, project packages, project folder (later wins a name, key or slot); project modules load only after the user trusts the project in /tools. Code runs with the user's privileges, not sandboxed.
  export default { name: "unique", tui(api) { ... }, daemon(api) { ... } }

Write it with customize_ui (in minimalist find it with tool_search; it only writes the user's flat extensions/ folder, names like look.ts, up to 64 KiB):
  {"action":"write","file":"look.ts","content":"<whole module>"}   {"action":"edit","file":"look.ts","old":"<unique text>","new":"..."}   {"action":"reload"}
The module is reloaded live, no restart. The result has errors (fix them with edit), terminalValidation (pending = no terminal acknowledged yet) and file.

tui(api), drawing and input:
- api.settings.get(key) / set(key, value) / set({...}): the profile keys of {{program}} docs customize.
- api.slot("footer.left|footer.right|footer.replace|header.replace|prompt.above|prompt.below", ctx => rows): rows are arrays of spans {text, fg, bg, bold, dim}; example in {{program}} docs footer.
- api.view(slot, input => rows | undefined): replace a built-in surface (message.user, message.assistant, tool.card, approval, topbar, sessions.sidebar, footer, home, slash.menu, page.status, ...). Pure and fast (4 ms); three faults turn the view off. List every slot: {{program}} view list; starter file: {{program}} view scaffold <slot>.
- api.renderMessage(role, ctx => rows), api.markdown(role, fn), api.messageStyle(role, {icon, label, lead, tint, layout}), api.prompt.chrome({lead, border, preset}), api.widget("tray"|"sidebar", id, {title, render}), api.page(id, {title, render}).
- api.key(key, run) binds a key live; api.command(name, description, (args, actions) => ...) adds a slash command; api.onStart(start) for processes, sockets and timers (runs after the old copy's api.onDispose finished, so a reload never runs two); api.onDispose(cleanup, may return a promise), api.redraw().
daemon(api): api.on("tool.before" | "tool.after" | "input" | "turn.end" | "prompt.system" | ..., handler), api.registerTool(tool), api.registerCommand({name, description, run}). cards.summary: review changes, commit, push, pull requests, worktrees (the Git page)
cards.text:
For: "show me the diff", "commit this", "open a pull request", "work in a separate worktree", "tell me when CI finishes".

The user's Git page: /git [changes|commit|worktrees|pr] (tier balanced; /tier git_hub). Tabs: Changes (/changes, alias /diff: review hunks, comment, send the review to the agent), Commit (tick files, confirm; never --no-verify, --amend, -a, or a push), Worktrees (/warp, /worktrees), PR. Setting git: git.defaultTab changes|commit|worktrees|pr, git.newSessionWorktree true makes /new and /bg start each session in a fresh worktree on a mend/ branch (from the current commit; uncommitted changes stay behind). Push, "publish to GitHub (private)" and "create pull request" use the user's own git and gh logins, so they stay off until the user types /experimental git_actions on. There is no model tool for them: for the agent, commit with git in the shell under the normal approvals (/commit starts a prompt that does it, and can push or open a PR), and never push unasked.

Model tools:
  review {action: summary|file|comment_add|comment_list|...}: reads the working tree and the user's review comments; it stages and edits nothing.
Commands the user types: /review (review changes in a subtask), /security-review and /bughunter (read-only, no edits), /pr comments (shows a pull request's review comments; /pr on|off switches PR watching and the reviewer), /verify (builds and tests the project).
  worktree {action: enter|exit|status|list|handoff|close}: off until the user turns on experimental.worktree_tool (full tier). enter makes a worktree on a new mend/<name> branch (naming: worktreeBranch) and moves this session into it mid-turn; every enter and exit needs the user's approval. Refused for a sub-agent, a session already in one, and while commands, children, a goal, a loop or a workflow run. Commit your work before leaving.
  pr_watch {action: watch|unwatch|list}: wakes the session only when a PR's checks fail or pass, someone comments, or it conflicts; needs experimental.pr_watch and gh; 5 watches per session. The user types /pr.

Limits: the Git page does not merge, close, tag, force-push, switch branch, stash or stage by hunk. Worktrees are cleaned only when merged, clean, unused and idle for worktreeGcDays days (off by default). Nothing makes a worktree per sub-agent. A folder that is not a repository shows only "Initialize repository".

Data honesty: branch, ahead/behind and dirty counts come from git itself in this folder; the PR tab reads gh. If gh is not logged in, say so.

Check: git status or the Git page header (branch, ahead, behind, dirty); say when you could not see the screen.

cards.text:
For: "work until all tests pass", "keep going until it is done", "show me a plan before touching anything", "track the steps".

Goal (one standing objective per session; the daemon starts each next turn itself until it ends):
  The user types /goal <objective> (optional --budget 50k tokens), /goal pause | resume | clear | edit | budget <n|off>. A goal ends complete, blocked, over budget, paused, or stopped by a provider usage limit.
  Model tools (main agent only, no approval): get_goal; create_goal {objective, token_budget?} only when the user explicitly asked for a goal; update_goal {status: complete|blocked|paused, note?}. complete only when every requirement is achieved and verified; blocked only after the same blocker held for 3 goal turns in a row; paused only if the user asked. Engines without these tools end their last message with GOAL_STATUS: complete or GOAL_STATUS: blocked - why.
  Not a loop: a loop recurs on a trigger in fresh sessions ({{program}} docs loops).

Todo: todo {items: [{text, status: pending|in_progress|done|cancelled, priority?}]} replaces the whole list ([] clears it, at most 50 items); keep one item in_progress. The user sees it in the dock (ctrl+t) and the right panel. In minimalist the plan and goal tools stay out of the request until the user turns on /tier plan_tools on.

Plan mode (read-only until approved): the user types /plan (/ultraplan plans and critiques without edits). The model calls plan_review {title?, markdown, phase?} (or plan_submit {plan}) with goal, steps with files, risks and how it will verify; plan_exit applies the reviewed plan. The user applies (enter), accepts without implementing (a), edits (e), comments (c) or rejects with a reason (r); /plan-review reopens saved decisions. Never edit files before approval. phase: "plan" means acceptance only. planExitAgent picks the agent that implements after approval (planExitAgent; build when unset).

Limits: one goal per session (an unfinished one needs the user's yes to be replaced); objective up to 60,000 characters (over 4,000 it is saved to a file and the goal reads it); the newest 20 goals per session are kept; a goal stalls, still active, after a failed or cancelled turn or two turns with no output, and restarts when the user sends a message or types /goal resume.

cards.text:
hooks.json in <data dir> (yours), in a package, or <project>/.mendcode/hooks.json (needs /tools trust). Re-read every turn.
  { "hooks": {
      "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "bash|write", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "./check.sh", "timeout": 10 } ] } ],
      "Stop": [ { "hooks": [ { "command": "npm test --silent" } ] } ] } }
- command is a string (run by /bin/sh -c) or an argv array (./x is relative to the folder holding hooks.json); the cwd is the session's project. timeout is seconds (default 15, max 120); a timed-out hook is killed and ignored.
- matcher is a case-insensitive regex tested against the whole tool name (and, for other events, the source, notification type or compaction trigger); empty or * matches all.
- The hook gets the event as JSON on stdin. Exit 0 continues. Exit 2 blocks where the event can: PreToolUse refuses the call (stderr is the error the model reads), UserPromptSubmit stops the prompt, Stop starts one follow-up turn with stderr (at most 3 in a row), PreCompact cancels the compaction. Stdout of a UserPromptSubmit hook that exits 0 is added to the prompt as context.
Events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, PermissionRequest (can only refuse, never approve), Notification, PreCompact, PostCompact. Tool, permission and compaction events apply to the native engine.

Hooks run with the user's privileges: write only what the user asked for. Check: the user sees every hook in /hooks; a bad file, unknown event or invalid matcher is listed there as a problem. Hooks in TypeScript: {{program}} docs extensions.

cards.summary: recurring work: every N minutes, daily, on an external trigger (loops)
cards.text:
For: "run this every 10 minutes", "every morning at 9 check X", "keep an eye on CI", "fire it from a script". A loop is recurring or long-running work: an objective, a trigger, a budget and a root session; each wake is a run, a normal message in a session with its own queue and approvals. One standing task in this session is a goal instead ({{program}} docs goals).

Model tool: loop {action: create|list|pause}. It is a write action (asks in ask and smart modes). Inspect existing loops first, and never set an iteration cap to zero. Loops the model creates are report-only (plan mode, nothing is edited) unless it sets reportOnly: false. Resume, stop, delete and accept stay with the user. Sub-agents do not get the tool.

Triggers (text form): manual · every 30m (1 minute to 30 days after the last run ended) · daily 09:00 or daily 09:00 Europe/Madrid (a missed window is not caught up) · adaptive 30m or adaptive 30m 5m..4h (doubles when a run found nothing, halves when it acted) · external (fired from outside: {{program}} loop fire <id> [--note text]).
Budget: monitor (never finishes by itself), goal (done when a stated condition holds, capped runs) or fixed.
Templates fill the rest: pr-watch (adaptive 15m, edits), ci-repair (every 10m), research-digest (adaptive 1h, report-only), repo-maintenance (every 30m).
Worktree: workspace worktree gives each run its own git worktree and branch loop/<name>-<id>-r<n>; a run that changed nothing leaves no trace, otherwise the branch stays for review. A report-only loop cannot use one. If no worktree can be made the run fails; it never falls back to the user's checkout.

The user's page: /loops (alias /loop): c new loop, t from a template, e edit, p pause or resume, n run now, a accept, s stop, d delete, f fire an external loop. From the user's shell (yours may only list and read; use the loop tool): {{program}} loop list [--all] | create [--every 1h|--daily 09:00] [--goal] [--runs N] "objective" | pause|resume|stop|run|delete <id> | fire <id>.

Metric experiments (feature autoresearch, full tier, on demand): the optional mendcode-autoresearch skill package, loaded by name, drives a loop that accepts a numeric improvement only when the correctness gates pass and the iteration, token and cost caps hold ({{program}} docs packages).
Not the same: pr_watch wakes a session with no model call only when a pull request changes ({{program}} docs git); the pr-watch loop template spends a model turn on every wake.

Limits: a paused, blocked or finished loop refuses a fire; edits to a running loop are refused until the run ends. Scheduling, the user daemon service, usage caps and the run ledger: {{program}} docs automation.

Check: the loop tool's list (or /loops) shows state, trigger and next wake. If the next wake is not shown, say it could not be read; do not state a time.

cards.summary: what the agent remembers: the memory tool, the /memory center, CLI
cards.text:
Durable facts the agent keeps across sessions, in three scopes: user (every project), project, session. Retrieval picks what is relevant for each message; what the agent sees is bounded.
Model tools: memory (status, categories, list, search, context, add, update, delete, propose) and memory_graph (overview, search, upsert_fact, link, validate); both are deferred (find them with tool_search) and writes are approved calls. Search before adding, update instead of duplicating, store only durable facts, never transient status, and never secrets. Proposals (propose) wait for the user in Pending, following per-category policies.
The user's page is /memory (tabs: Pending, Saved, Archived, Dream, Graph, Policies, Evolution, Extraction, Sharing): approve or reject proposals, edit, archive, change scope, pin. Dream is the daily consolidation pass; its time and policies are set there.
CLI (add, edit, delete, apply, reject: the user's terminal; refused from your shell): {{program}} memory [status] | preview [query] | list [--status saved|pending|archived] | search "query" [--limit N] | add [--user] [--category C] "text" | edit <id> "text" [--scope global|project] | delete|apply|reject <id>. Add --dir D for another data dir.
Defaults: using saved facts in the prompt and generating them after a turn are both OFF until the user turns them on; approval of generated facts is ON. Settings (user's /settings or the /memory tabs; never change them yourself): memoryEnabled gates proposals and retrieval; memoryUse injects saved facts into the prompt; memoryGenerate extracts after a turn; memoryRequireApproval sends extractions to Pending. cards.summary: several sessions in one checkout, no worktrees
cards.text:
For: "can I run several sessions on the same repo", "do I need a worktree per agent", "what is this [one tree] line", "someone else changed this file".

What it is ([[feature:one_tree]], balanced and full; /tier one_tree off|on): sessions in the same folder share it. The daemon remembers which files each session wrote in the last 30 minutes. When a tool result names one of another session's files (git status, git diff, a failing test or typecheck), or you write one, the result ends with one line:
  [one tree] Other sessions are changing these files in this checkout: <path> («<their session title>», <age>). ...
Nothing is added while a session works alone; a file is named to you at most once every 10 minutes.

When you see the line: those changes are another session's work in progress, not the user's and not yours. Do not revert, "fix", reformat or commit them. Commit only the files you changed (git add <your files>, never git add -A). A failure in one of their files is theirs: say so, and do not chase it.

Engines: the native engine and Claude Code (through a PostToolUse hook) report their calls; native sub-agents and Claude Code's own sub-agents count as writers of their own. Codex, ACP agents and pi do not yet.

Not possible: locking a file against another session; merging two sessions' edits of the same file; seeing other machines' sessions.

A package is a folder with mendcode-package.json that carries any of: skills/ commands/ agents/ tools/ themes/ extensions/ hooks mcp.json keybindings, and optionally a whole look (activate: theme, tuiProfile, views, keybindings). Disabling or removing one puts everything back; your own settings win over a package's.
  mendcode-package.json: { "name": "acme", "version": "1.0.0", "description": "..." }   (name: lowercase letters, digits, . _ - and equal to the folder name; also author, homepage, license)
Commands (add --project for this project's .mendcode/packages; else user scope; your shell: only new, check, list):
  {{program}} package new <name> [--dir PARENT]     scaffold a complete, commented package that already loads
  {{program}} package check [folder]                validate without running anything (schema, compatibility, capabilities, forbidden keys, size)
  {{program}} package install <folder|github:owner/repo#ref|git:URL|npm:name@x.y.z> [--replace]   refuses links, secrets and trees over 2000 files or 20 MB
  {{program}} package list | config [name] | enable|disable <name> [--switch] | remove <name> [--purge] | restore <name>
  {{program}} packages create   snapshots this project's .mendcode/ (own setup: docs profile)
To try one, write it straight into <project>/.mendcode/packages/<name>/ or <data dir>/packages/<name>/; no restart.
In chat, the packages tool (find it with tool_search) does list, info, search, check (read-only) and install, enable, disable, switch-look, remove, new (each needs an approval card, even in full permission mode; install takes only an exact name from a configured local source). One package owns the look per scope; switch-look says which.
The approval card of a big package is a summary: files and size per folder, the largest files, and every script, hook, tool definition and executable listed in full. Over 2000 files, 20 MB, 12 folder levels or 150 runnable files the tool refuses and names the limit, what it measured and the shell command to run instead (for example {{program}} package enable <name> [--switch]); do not retry the tool, give the user that command.
Features (balanced): package_tools (the packages tool above); package_capabilities (the user's /marketplace preview shows declared capabilities and static hints from a bounded scan; absent hints never prove safety); official_packages (the examples/official-packages catalog, added by the user as a source: mendcode-review, mendcode-autoresearch, mendcode-web-routing, all on-demand skills). Catalogs never contact a service on their own. A user's keep or override of a package is recorded in activation.json. Turned off: disabledPackages, disabledPackageResources.
A package cannot change permissions, trust, credentials, budgets, models, sandbox, hooks or MCP through activate; the manifest fails the schema if it tries. The user manages packages in /packages (o lists what a package overrides, p the precedence report). Install only what the user asked for.

cards.summary: permission modes, approvals, allow and deny rules, the OS sandbox
cards.text:
Every tool call is read, write or execute. Modes (per session; the default for new sessions is the defaultPermission setting):
  ask: asks for writes and commands | edits: runs edits, asks for commands | smart: runs low-risk calls by fixed rules, asks about the rest | full: runs unless a deny rule matches | plan: read-only until a plan is approved
Reads of .env files ask in every mode. "For this session" approves that tool for the session. Deny rules always win. A denied call is the user's decision: adapt, never retry it. Package changes need an approval card even in full.
Smart mode runs reads, edits inside the project, and allow-listed commands (ls, cat, grep, read-only git, the project's own test and build commands, and mendcode docs [--search] words on its own line). It asks for destructive commands, secrets paths, .git and .mendcode paths, anything outside the project, network, loops, unlisted commands and $ or backtick expansion; it refuses rm -r of / or ~ and similar outright. Every prompt says why it asks.

Change (your shell's change commands and --approve are refused in all modes; when the user asks, propose it with mendcode_settings, e.g. {"defaultPermission":"edits"}, saved on their Apply):
  shift+tab or the permission picker changes the current session; {{program}} control-plane permissions status
  {{program}} control-plane permissions set-default approval|smart|full_access|ask|edits|full     new sessions
  {{program}} control-plane permissions set-reviewer-role <model role>     optional reviewer of uncertain smart calls (off by default)
Rules and allow list are daemon settings in the user's /settings: permission (ordered tool and path rules, ask/deny/allow) and permissionAllow (command prefixes such as ["make test","git commit"]; they never override a risk rule or the forbidden list). Remote clients cannot.
Sandbox (opt-in, shell commands of the model run inside an OS sandbox; approvals still apply): /sandbox off | read-only | workspace-write, /sandbox network on|off, /sandbox allow <abs path>. Setting sandbox: { "mode": "workspace-write", "network": "off", "writableRoots": [] }.
Trust: a project's tools, hooks, MCP servers, agents and extensions run only after the user trusts the directory in /tools or /trust. Never widen permissions, the sandbox or trust unless the user asked for that exact change.
A rejection ends the turn unless the experimental flag continue_loop_on_deny is on. The user's commands: /permissions lists grants and modes, /approve allows one retry of a call that was denied (you may suggest it, never assume it). Extra settings: additionalDirectories (outside folders that count as the workspace: no external-directory ask, writable in the sandbox); smartSandboxTrust (smart mode runs unknown shell commands without asking only when the sandbox is on with network off); engineSafetyPrompts (Claude Code still asks when its own safety check flags a command in full access); permissionReviewerRole.

cards.summary: PR reviewer, repo watch, hosted Action, @mendcode
cards.text:
For: "review this PR", "why did MendCode comment on my PR", "configure the reviewer", "teach the reviewer".

A review has two passes in plan-mode child sessions: one finds candidate defects as JSON (line on the diff's new side, severity, category, file:line evidence), a fresh one tries to refute each. Only confirmed findings are published (strict also publishes plausible ones), ranked, at most `cap` (8); the rest are one "and N smaller notes" line. Context is the diff plus the code graph's callers and callees of each changed symbol, within half of budget.tokens_per_pr (200000).

Repo config .mendcode/review.yaml: enabled (false), profile quiet|normal|strict, cap 1..30, paths [{glob, instructions}], ignore, checks (run in the OS sandbox, no network, output to the verifier), fixes, triggers, budget. The base branch decides everything but path instructions, so a PR cannot turn checks or publishing on for itself. Learnings: .mendcode/review-learnings.md, one bullet each, read from the base branch, cut to 4 KB.

Switch: off until experimental.pr_review (feature pr_review, balanced tier up, permit). The user types /pr review [pr] (one PR now), /pr watch-repo (a new PR or new head starts a review; no model call while nothing changes), /pr unwatch-repo, /pr repos, /pr publish on|off (asked once before the first post to a repository). Posts are one COMMENT review with inline comments and hidden markers, never twice for the same finding or head. State: <dir>/pr-review/watches.json and one file per PR.

PR comments (write access only): @mendcode review | pause | resume | explain (reply to a MendCode comment) | fix (needs fixes: true; local daemon only; pushes one commit only if checks pass) | learn <text> (proposes the learnings line). A failing check on a reviewed head gets one explaining comment per failing set.

Hosted: `mendcode github install --hosted --model PROVIDER/MODEL --release TAG --sha256 HEX [--write]` writes .github/workflows/mendcode-review.yml (ubuntu-latest, pull_request never pull_request_target, the provider key secret plus GITHUB_TOKEN with pull-requests: write). It runs `github run --publish --review`, state from GitHub markers, no checks. A fork's run has no secret and says a maintainer can comment `@mendcode review`.

Data honesty: say which findings were confirmed and which were folded; never call a finding verified when the summary says verification failed.

cards.summary: prompt modes (how much MendCode text each call carries) and model families
cards.text:
A prompt mode picks how much MendCode text rides in every model call: minimal, focus, guide, full, custom.
  minimal: a small boundary, the one-line pointer to these cards, the user's instructions and memories
  focus (default): adds the native coding harness, the skill catalog and a one-line note for the model family

  full: adds the operator note about MendCode itself and the family's context files
  custom: reads <project>/.mendcode/prompts/custom.md (a regular file, up to 32 KiB, {{cwd}} expands) and inherits nothing else
The family is auto, codex, claude, gemini, kimi, deepseek, mistral, glm, minimax, grok, local; auto follows the session's model on every call, naming one overrides it. A family changes guidance only, never provider, model, permissions or budgets. Instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) ride in every mode.

cards.text:
For: "make it think harder", "lower the effort to save tokens", "what is JEV / adaptive reasoning".

Effort is per session and per model: the levels a model supports (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh). The user sets it in /model (F3 steps it); a headless run takes --effort LEVEL ({{program}} docs automation). A level the model lacks is refused, not rounded. You cannot change your own effort.

Adaptive effort (JEV; feature jev, tier full; experimental flag reasoning_auto; off by default). Two parts, both the user's:
  The evaluator policy: /model reasoning (or a in /model) opens a grid: o off, s shadow (evaluates, keeps the baseline effort), a adaptive (applies supported efforts to native main and plan generations); c toggles consent for evaluator processing, p picks the evaluator provider (OpenRouter by default). Consent is stored under the data dir (consent.json); a project's .mendcode/adaptive-reasoning.json can only reduce the mode and limits, never grant consent. Turning it on sends data to an evaluator provider: never do it yourself.
  The tool: with the flag on, reasoning_auto lets the model ask for one higher effort for the current turn only, capped at high, with reason verification_failed or technical_block and 1 to 1000 characters of concrete evidence. Network errors, permission requests and unrelated failures are not reasons. Manual effort, named variants and provider parameters always win.

cards.summary: drive MendCode from a phone or another machine; share a session; editors
cards.text:
For: "control it from my phone", "attach to the daemon on my server", "send someone a link to this session", "connect my editor". Each is off until the user turns it on; none starts by itself.

Phone (Telegram): the user creates a bot with @BotFather and gives the daemon the token as MENDCODE_TELEGRAM_TOKEN or a mode-600 file <data dir>/telegram-token (never through a slash command or flag, never in chat). Then /remote-control on, /remote-control pair (an 8-character code valid 10 minutes), and in a private chat the user sends the bot "pair CODE" as the bot's own pair command. /remote-control shows state, off stops it, unpair removes chats. State is <data dir>/channels.json (mode 0600; paired chats, never the token); Console state is console.json. Approvals arrive as buttons.

Another machine (token create and revoke, console setup and share are the user's; refused from your shell): on the server {{program}} remote token create --dir DATA --name laptop (the token prints once; list and revoke exist), start the daemon with --listen 127.0.0.1:9876 (a non-loopback host needs --tls-cert and --tls-key; there is no insecure switch), then on the client {{program}} --connect HOST:PORT --token-file PATH. Read-only tokens are refused for writes. No listener exists by default. Remote and peer clients cannot change permissions, ACP agents or other host-local settings.

Share a session (Console, off by default): /share (Enter creates or syncs, u unshares), /unshare, policy disabled|manual|auto in the same page (share). A link holds user and assistant text with credentials redacted; no local paths, attachments, reasoning or tool output. Needs a configured Console origin and token file ({{program}} console setup URL --token-file PATH); /org switches organization; /console manages accounts. No public backend is chosen for the user. Changing policy never shares old sessions.

Editors: /ide on reads the open file, cursor and selection from Zed (read-only; files inside the project only; over 1 MiB refused). For JetBrains or Zed as an agent host, point them at the command `mendcode acp`. There is no JetBrains plugin.

Rooms and terminals: /mflow (rooms, peers, file leases between agents), /tsm (terminal-session adapter for cmux, kitty, ghostty, wezterm); both are opt-in managers with a status and doctor under {{program}} control-plane mflow|tsm.

Say what is not on: if a feature is off, tell the user the switch above; do not edit remote.json, tokens or Console settings yourself.

cards.summary: API keys, tokens and passwords: markers, the /env vault, chat encryption
cards.text:
For: "save my API key", "use this token in a command", "the key leaked into the chat", "encrypt my chats", "environment variables for the model's commands".

Commands (the user types them): /secrets manages pasted secrets, /env named credentials, /privacy chat encryption.
The rule: never ask for a secret in chat, never print one, never write one to a file or a command line. The user types a key in /connect (a provider) or /env (any named credential); a secret that was pasted in a message becomes a marker ‹secret:N› before the model or the transcript sees it.

Pasted secrets: the model sees only ‹secret:N›. To use one, write the marker in a shell command or in the content of write, edit or apply_patch; MendCode puts the real value in just before the tool runs, after the user approves, and hides it again in the output. The secrets tool lists markers and credential names (never values). Detected shapes: provider keys, GitHub, AWS, Slack, Google, Stripe, JWT, PEM keys, user:password@ URLs, Bearer headers, and NAME=value where the name holds SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, API_KEY.

Named credentials, /env (hidden from tier minimalist; /tier balanced shows it): a adds a name and a hidden value, ctrl+s picks scope (project default, session, global), i imports a dotenv inside the project after a preview of names only, e replaces, x removes. Session overrides project overrides global. In the native engine the model sees the names and built-in shell and shell_session processes (background included) receive the values as environment variables: use os.environ["NAME"], never print it. New values reach new processes only. The vault is encrypted on disk; no tool reveals a value. Claude Code, Codex, pi and ACP get the values in their process environment too (names in their prompt), but no masking; setting engineEnvironment false keeps them native-only.

Chat encryption, /privacy (off by default): p then y encrypts the local database, attachments and saved tool output; ordinary cat, grep and SQLite readers can no longer read them. Turning it off restores plain files.

If a key was exposed: tell the user to revoke it at the provider and add the new one with /env or /connect. Masking is a net, not a reason to paste secrets.

Not possible: reading a secret's value, exporting the vault, injecting into custom or overridden tools, a model tool that sets a credential.

Check: the secrets tool lists the name; the command that uses it prints ‹env:NAME› instead of the value. Say so if you could not run it.

What it reports (times in the machine's local zone, which it names):
  turns: count by status (completed, cancelled, failed, running), each one's real start, end and duration; the longest are listed with their tokens.

  per day and per hour: active minutes, turns started, output and cache-read tokens. A turn's time and usage are split over the hours it ran, so a 9-hour turn shows in each of its hours. The last 72 active hours are listed.

  unknown: ended turns with no recorded usage are counted as unknown, not zero; "partial" turns ended before the engine's own total and carry the sum of the calls it reported.
  sub-agents (Claude Code's agents): runs, their tool calls, tokens and time (they can run in parallel, so their time can exceed the turn's).
  tools: calls by name with errors, and calls made by sub-agents; child sessions with their usage.

cards.summary: where settings and config files live, and who may change what
cards.text:
Data dir: ~/.mendcode-v2, or the daemon's --dir / MENDCODE_V2_DIR. It holds AGENTS.md (global instructions), mcp.json, hooks.json, keybindings.json, statusline.json, tui/profile.json (terminal look) and the folders extensions/ skills/ commands/ agents/ tools/ themes/ packages/. The daemon's own settings live in its database there (mendd.db): never edit it.
Project: <project>/.mendcode/ holds the same kinds of files, plus project.json (project-level settings; an unreadable one is listed in /debug-config), prompts/custom.md and context/project.md. AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md at the project root are read as instructions. Project tools, hooks, MCP, agents and extensions wait for the user to trust the project (/tools).
Layers, lowest to highest: user packages, user folder, project packages, project folder. A later layer wins a name.

Two kinds of settings:
1. Terminal look (theme, density, prompt box, logo, footer, ...): the profile. Apply with customize_ui {"action":"settings","values":{...}} (find a key: action keys); keys: {{program}} docs customize.
2. Daemon settings (tier, permissions, models, budgets, compaction, ...): you CAN change any. mendcode_settings {"action":"get"} reads them (no secrets); {"action":"propose","patch":{...},"reason":"..."} validates the patch (a key's value replaces it whole; null resets it), shows the user before → after, and saves only on their Apply, in every mode. Do not tell the user to do it. Your shell's change commands are refused. The user has /settings, /tier, /model, /experimental. Cards: {{program}} docs permissions | models | tiers | budgets | compaction.

Read the current state, never guess it, and not from a MendCode source tree on this machine (it may be another version): mendcode_settings get; {{program}} status; {{program}} control-plane system config-layers (every layer, no secrets); config-paths. The user has /debug-config and /doctor.
Common daemon keys: tier, defaultPermission, outputStyle, budgets, experimental, foreignResources (.agents and .claude folders as data).
Others: /init sets up the instructions file; instructionFallbacks (extra instruction file names) and projectRootMarkers (.git when unset); shell (the model's shell; per project too), shellCommandPrefix (run before each command) and loginShell; instructions (extra instruction paths or globs); watcher { ignore: [globs] }; tool_output { max_lines, max_bytes, filters }; logLevel; autoupdate, enterprise; setupPreset, onboarded; profiles (per-folder memories, roles, permission; {{program}} profile add NAME DIR) and projectThemes ({{program}} docs theme). Turned-off extras: disabledPackages, disabledPackageResources, disabledExtensions, disabledSkills.
Remote and peer terminals cannot set permission, sandbox, shellEnvironment, trustedToolDirs, proxy or projectConfig (nor approve such a proposal). Propose only what the user asked; never raise or remove a spend limit unless asked for that exact change. Never print or ask for secrets.

A skill is instructions for a kind of task: <data dir>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (every project) or <project>/.mendcode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (that project). MendCode also reads .agents/skills and .claude/skills as data. Nothing ships built in.

cards.summary: run sub-agents in parallel or background; continue, list, pause, stop
cards.text:
For: "run two agents in parallel", "keep working while it runs", "pause / stop the agent", "continue that agent". A sub-agent is a child session with its own context (task tool). Writing one: {{program}} docs agents.

Model tools (feature subagents, tier balanced; the live lines say if they are on here):
  task {description, prompt, background?, task_id?, agent?, model?, isolation?}: foreground waits; background: true returns a task_id at once. The child cannot see this chat: give the whole prompt and what to return. The description names subagentCatalog (6) agents; agent: "?" lists all. explore is read-only and returns locations with evidence.
  isolation: "worktree" (feature task_worktree, full tier): the child works in a git worktree of HEAD; its changes end on branch mend/task-<id> (in its result), never merged.
  fork: true (task_fork, opt-in): the child starts from this chat on your model (cached), rereads it each call; prompt only the task.
  Parallel: several task calls with background: true. Each end arrives by itself (subagentOwnerWake, on). Do not poll.
  task_status {action: list|get|wait|cancel, task_id, timeout_ms}: list, read one, wait once (30 s, max 300 s), cancel for good.
  Continue a finished child with its task_id (context kept); with model it goes on on that model (after a usage limit, or cheaper). Not while running.
In a Claude Code or Codex session their own Agent tool cannot change a child's model; delegate_task can (full tier, the user runs /tier thread_mcp on claude; {{program}} docs engines).
A user prompt opening with @name of a child agent goes to that child (queued while it works, kept in <data dir>/agent-mentions.json; agentMentions).
Children inherit your permission mode (lowered by their agent's cap), work in your directory unless isolated, and lack main-only tools (question, loop, worktree). Two children editing one file clash: split by file.
Model: task's, agent's, subagent role, else (cheap_subagents, balanced) your provider's mid tier under a large one (Sol → Luna, Opus → Sonnet; Claude Code too), else yours.

Limits (a call over one fails by name: wait or continue a task_id, do not retry in a loop):
  subagentDepth 1 (0 turns task off) · subagentMaxChildren 4 running per parent · subagentMaxDescendants 16 per tree · 256 started per tree.

The user controls (no model tool): /pause [id] finishes the turn, holds the queue; /unpause; /stop [id] cancels it and every child. /tasks lists children (x cancel, b detach, w wait); /bg detaches to Agent View; /tree.

Retries replay the result (orchestration_receipts); /panel galaxy draws the tree (panel_orbit).

Does not exist: a pause tool for the model; a worktree per child by default; a scratch folder per child (/scratch is one note per project); merging children's edits. /fanout compares models. engine: claude|codex|pi|acp:<name> for a child needs the full tier.

Check: a task result names its task_id and state. No notice: say so, do not guess.

cards.text:
For: "ask my other session", "what is the other chat doing", "hand this off to a fresh session", "side question without polluting this chat".

Model tools (same project only; text only, secrets never cross; never offered to remote clients):
  sessions {limit?}: this project's other sessions (id, title, state). A recent chat is not an agent running now.
  tell {sessionId, text, mode?}: a self-contained message to one session by its exact id from sessions (never from a title). The answer returns by itself as a notice: do not poll. Writes need approval; mode steer joins its running turn after the next tool result and never interrupts.

The user types: @thread:<id> in the prompt appends a read-only snapshot of that session (last request, last 6 messages, at most 3 mentions); /handoff <goal> (tier balanced) starts a focused child session with a redacted summary and the goal in its draft, sent only when the user sends it; /btw <question> opens a side chat that sees the last ~24,000 characters of this session but runs no tools and is not part of the transcript, export or compaction; /btw clear empties it.

Not possible: reading another project's sessions; a message that interrupts a running turn; creating or launching sessions from a tool; sharing files or permissions with another session.

cards.summary: feature tiers: minimalist, balanced, full, and per-feature switches
cards.text:
One tier setting (minimalist|balanced|full) selects a bundle of switches that already exist; with no tier set nothing changes. A tier sets the chat view, density and the project's prompt mode once when applied (minimalist: minimal, balanced: focus, full: full), and turns feature modules on or off live. Every feature stays individually switchable.
The user changes it: /tier lists the bundles and what is on now and why; /tier minimalist|balanced|full applies one and says what it added or removed; /tier <feature> on|off|default overrides one feature; /tier off clears it; the Tier row of /setup. The daemon refuses tier changes from remote terminals. No CLI command writes it; when the user asks, propose it with mendcode_settings ({"tier":"full"} or {"features":{...}}, the whole object), saved only on the user's Apply.
What differs (the user's /tier shows the exact list for this version): minimalist keeps the lean coding core of tools in every request and the rest behind tool_search, with the smallest prompt; balanced adds sub-agents, the code graph, script workflows, the orientation block and output filters; full adds MCP, plan tools, pets and adaptive reasoning. Risky features (computer control, browser, voice) are never turned on by a tier: they need their own switch.
